items.headline: Zuckerberg's Muse Now Builds Your Own Mini Apps
items.excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg previews Muse's Spaces tool, which tracks your other apps in the background, as critics warn Meta's agent already reaches too far.

items.headline: US Officials Tie Jensen Huang to Alleged Chinese Spy
items.excerpt: A new account says the Nvidia chief's tie to an accused Chinese spy was romantic, as the executive linked to him reportedly vanished months ago.

items.headline: Trillions, Task Forces and Trimmed Targets
items.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic both land under their funding targets, the Justice Department opens an AI task force, and auditors flag redacted evidence at Anthropic.

items.headline: Anthropic Pays the AP, Battles the Rest
items.excerpt: Anthropic paid the AP for election data as its fight with four Canadian publishers over free use drags on.

items.headline: Information and Finance Jobs Shrink as AI Blame Fades
items.excerpt: October's jobs report found growth in professional services and computer work, but the sectors AI reaches deepest, information and finance, kept losing jobs.

items.headline: PitchBook Values Databricks at $68.7 Billion
items.excerpt: PitchBook's own model prices the business at $68.7 billion, about a third of the $190 billion its investors just paid.

items.headline: Google Cuts AI Video Price, Skips Some Instructions
items.excerpt: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash drops to 7 cents a second and stretches clips to 15 seconds, but one review still routes real work elsewhere.

items.headline: Hidden Anthropic Model Cracks an 18-Year Quantum Puzzle
items.excerpt: A secretive Anthropic model helped a tiny lab prove a quantum computing conjecture open since 2008, and only the proof itself is public.

items.headline: Investors Tell Anthropic Its IPO Price Is Too High
items.excerpt: Major investors want Anthropic's $1.5 trillion IPO value cut toward $1 trillion after Thursday's stock selloff.

items.headline: Spies, Slides and Shopping Bots That Still Buy Wrong
items.excerpt: Congress presses Nvidia over a Chinese tie, chip stocks lose $440 billion in a day, and Visa's AI shoppers still buy the wrong thing.

items.headline: Claude Code's Email Leak Exposes Anthropic's Bug Backlog
items.excerpt: A privacy bug sent user emails to websites for months while 98.2 percent of Anthropic's bug reports sat unassigned.

items.headline: Nvidia Calls an Alleged Spy a Customer
items.excerpt: Three House chairmen want Jensen Huang to explain his ties to Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive Nvidia calls an ordinary customer.

items.headline: Gold Explorers Point AI at the Safest Ground
items.excerpt: Gold exploration money increasingly aims AI at ground miners already hold, while hunts for brand-new deposits hit a record low.

items.headline: Disney's OpenAI Deal Collapses Before One Check Clears
items.excerpt: Disney promised OpenAI $1 billion for Sora access to its characters, and OpenAI killed the app three months later with $0 of it paid.

items.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic Expand H-1B Hiring as Rivals Retreat
items.excerpt: AI labs more than tripled H-1B filings under Trump's $100,000 fee while Amazon, Google and Microsoft pulled back, and two courts just blocked the charge.

items.headline: OpenAI Locks Its Strongest Hacking Model Away
items.excerpt: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber doubles its own model's price, demands a security review, and still misses more than half its benchmark's attacks.

items.headline: Microsoft Ends Its Oracle AI Cloud Deal
items.excerpt: Microsoft dropped a 2023 deal for Oracle's aging AI chips, and Oracle says buyers still want them at a premium.

items.headline: Cat Wu Quits Claude Code for OpenAI
items.excerpt: Cat Wu left Anthropic's Claude Code team and joined OpenAI days later, one of three Claude Code departures since Oct. 24.

items.headline: Moonshot Gives Away Its Biggest Model
items.excerpt: Moonshot released the full weights behind its 2.8 trillion parameter Kimi K3.1 Pro, free to run and sell, with one catch.

items.headline: Schools, Spending and a Skeptic's Spreadsheet
items.excerpt: Google ties school search to its AI, Michael Burry calls Anthropic's growth math pure optimism, and voters punish AI's biggest campaign spenders.

items.headline: Pentagon's AI Billions Bypass Its Smallest Suppliers
items.excerpt: The Pentagon's record AI budget flows to contractors already wired for audits, while a suspended rule leaves small suppliers outside the same systems.

items.headline: Judge Lee Keeps Anthropic's $3 Billion Case Alive
items.excerpt: Judge Eumi Lee dropped Dario Amodei's personal copyright claim but left Anthropic's bigger fight over Claude's lyrics unresolved.

items.headline: Oracle's OpenAI Bet Drags Its Credit Toward Junk
items.excerpt: S&P cut Oracle one notch above junk after OpenAI's deal grew to half its backlog, and bondholders say Oracle hid the math.

items.headline: Aina Charges $399 for What Rabbit Just Dropped
items.excerpt: Aina's new ring costs $399 to $499, the same hardware bet that sank Humane's Pin and that Rabbit dropped this September.

items.headline: AI Super PACs Back Seven Losers
items.excerpt: Leading the Future and Public First funded twelve competitive Nov. 3 races, and the side AI money backed lost in seven of them.

items.headline: Ansari's AI Ban Post Sinks Storage Stocks
items.excerpt: Rep. Yassamin Ansari's call to ban superintelligence helped drive Western Digital's stock down 13.5 percent, and three rival storage makers fell with it.

items.headline: Claude Starts Reading Bank Accounts, Stays Read-Only
items.excerpt: Anthropic's new Claude feature reads a bank balance and two years of spending, but security researchers say read-only access still leaves a risk standing.

items.headline: Twelve Machines Called the Senate. Inside BULX the Morning After.
items.excerpt: BULX's twelve agents backed Democrats at 64% before they won the Senate, and Nathan Scherner says what that proved.

items.headline: Wells Fargo Makes Customers Prove They Revoked AI Access
items.excerpt: A contract change effective Nov. 24 keeps customers liable for an AI agent's trades until they document that they shut it off.

items.headline: Altman Says Humans Must Keep Control Over AI
items.excerpt: Altman says people must always stay in control of AI's future.

items.headline: Alphabet's Numbers Test Warsh's Rate Warning
items.excerpt: Kevin Warsh says rates still reach AI investment, and Alphabet's same-day earnings, funded by new debt and equity, become the test case.

items.headline: Self-Improvement, Shareholders and a Sovereign Stake
items.excerpt: Anthropic warns regulators its AI may soon improve itself, an Alphabet investor sues over stolen songs, and Canada buys a stake in Cohere.

items.headline: Voters Punish Data Centers as AI Backlash Spreads
items.excerpt: Voters in ten states banned or restricted AI data centers Nov. 3, and a $125 million industry campaign barely slowed them.

items.headline: Anthropic Tells the SEC It May Improve Itself
items.excerpt: Anthropic's amended IPO filing tells federal regulators its AI may soon help build a smarter version of itself.

items.headline: Hyperscalers Buy the Fiber Rural Broadband Needs
items.excerpt: AI data centers are buying up the fiber and the crews that rural broadband needs, pushing the federal connection promise further behind schedule.

items.headline: Micron's $27 Billion Chip Bet Still Squeezes Buyers
items.excerpt: Micron spent $27.37 billion chasing AI memory demand in fiscal 2026, and buyers like Framework Computer are still paying the shortage's price.

items.headline: Suno Pays Record Labels, and Fights the Musicians
items.excerpt: Suno signed opt-in deals with Warner and BMG, then asked a judge to dismiss the suit from four musicians left outside both deals.

items.headline: ChatGPT, Claude and Meta AI Remember You Unevenly
items.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic promise a deleted memory clears within 30 days, and Meta keeps its own window private.

items.headline: Google and Anthropic Have Owned AI's Top Spot
items.excerpt: Across a year of leaderboard history, only two labs ever reached #1, and buyers who watch price say the chase misses the point.

items.headline: Musk Jokes About Space Data Centers as Stocks Slip
items.excerpt: Elon Musk joked about moving data centers to space after Tuesday's vote, and data center stocks slipped at Wednesday's open.

items.headline: Game Studios Rate Their Own AI a 3 of 10
items.excerpt: A 101-leader survey finds 94 percent of game studios already use AI, yet most call their own integration shallow.

items.headline: Claude Maps First 3D Vault Particle From Bacteria
items.excerpt: Anthropic used Claude to map a hidden cell structure, and a congresswoman demanded an AI pause the same afternoon.

items.headline: VRChat Rejects the Label 95% of Users Backed
items.excerpt: VRChat's own survey found 95 percent of users wanted an AI-content label. The company declined, and Steam's rating fell fast.

items.headline: Cursor Owes Developers a Backdoor Explanation
items.excerpt: Five days after a trojanized Claude Code extension reached up to 5,000 developers, Cursor's public notice still skips how the attacker got in.

items.headline: Revolut Swaps Claude Code for a Cheaper Open Model
items.excerpt: Revolut moved 2,000 engineers off Claude Code and Codex onto a self-hosted open model, cutting its AI coding costs sharply.

items.headline: Caution, Compute and a Capital Bet
items.excerpt: Goldman Sachs pulls its AI coding tools back to engineers, Nvidia caps cloud partners' China sales, and Abu Dhabi doubles down on OpenAI.

items.headline: Embark Re-Records Arc Raiders After AI Backlash
items.excerpt: Embark Studios swapped AI-generated quest dialogue for human voice actors in Arc Raiders, months after a Eurogamer review called the AI voices mediocre.

items.headline: Chatbots Pick Restaurants, and Chains Keep Winning
items.excerpt: AI recommendation engines name the same few restaurant chains again and again, leaving most independent restaurants out of the answer.

items.headline: OpenAI Hires Dan Driscoll for Pentagon Access
items.excerpt: A former Army Secretary who clashed with the Pentagon's own defense chief now sells OpenAI's case to the government he just left.

items.headline: Publishers License AI for Millions, Then Sue for More
items.excerpt: News Corp, the Guardian and Reach license AI content for tens of millions, while the Times, USA Today and Canadian papers sue for much more.

items.headline: Otter and Granola Face Suits Over Hidden Recording
items.excerpt: Two of the four leading AI meeting notetakers face federal privacy suits, while Fireflies warns every attendee by default and Fathom shows a visible banner.

items.headline: Meituan Undercuts Claude's Price, Skips the Proof
items.excerpt: Meituan's LongCat-2.5 undercuts Claude's price by a wide margin, while its benchmark claims and promised open weights both await independent confirmation.

items.headline: Honnibal Calls Astra's Weight Edit Misleading
items.excerpt: A viral post said GPT-6 Astra edited Qwen's weights directly; spaCy's Matthew Honnibal says the test mostly ran Python code.

items.headline: Wells Fargo Needs Proof You Fired Your AI
items.excerpt: Its new agreement, effective Nov. 24, keeps customers liable for an AI agent's trades until they can show, with evidence, that they shut it off.

items.headline: Xiaomi's Humanoid Robot Clocks Its First 8-Hour Shift
items.excerpt: Xiaomi's robot worked eight hours straight at a 90 percent task, apart from the separate 98 percent job its headlines borrowed.

items.headline: Claude and Grok Will Mark Your Text by Saturday
items.excerpt: Anthropic adds its text watermark to four older Claude models Tuesday, and xAI turns one on for seven Grok API models Saturday.

items.headline: Strata's Code Already Beats Altman's DRAM Claim
items.excerpt: A free local AI engine fills a home PC's memory the way Altman says data centers should, even as OpenAI drives the shortage.

items.headline: Karpathy Builds HackerTube With Claude in Two Hours
items.excerpt: One programmer says Claude sorted 43 million Hacker News comments into a working video site in two hours, faster than most teams plan a sprint.

items.headline: Tests, Trillions and a Trip to Seoul
items.excerpt: A benchmark humbles every AI agent, Aramco pours $2.6 billion into Saudi Arabia's AI champion, and Sam Altman flies to Seoul chasing memory chips.

items.headline: Cathie Wood Buys Tempus Stock Before Its Beat
items.excerpt: ARK Invest added to an already top-three stake in Tempus AI two days before the company topped revenue estimates and narrowed its loss.

items.headline: Beef Packers Blame Cattle, Then Add AI
items.excerpt: America's layoff tracker added a reason called Cattle Shortage this year, and the same packers scaling AI yield systems chose where its costs landed.

items.headline: Elvis Estate Sues Anthropic for $48.6 Million
items.excerpt: Rights holders for 274 Elvis Presley songs say Anthropic trained Claude on scraped lyrics, the second music lawsuit filed against it in two days.

items.headline: Jumper and Dean Trade Results for Unproven Labs
items.excerpt: Nobel laureate John Jumper left DeepMind for Anthropic, and three Google veterans founded Discovery Loop, betting on focused labs over famous ones.

items.headline: Musk Blames Costs for Grok Bot's Usage Limits
items.excerpt: Elon Musk capped Grok Bot's heaviest users days after calling its growth the fastest he had ever seen.

items.headline: Tao Calls Grad Training Math's Top AI Risk
items.excerpt: A UK report says mathematicians stay essential to AI; Tao says the real emergency is training the next ones fast enough.

items.headline: Can an AI Committee Tell the Future?
items.excerpt: BULX's twelve AI agents gave Democrats a 64% Senate chance on Election Eve, while Kalshi paid 75% and Decision Desk HQ said 65%.

items.headline: GPT-6 Astra Edits Qwen's Weights, Skips Training
items.excerpt: MIT researchers had GPT-6 Astra edit a smaller model's weights directly, and Anthropic's own filing flagged how fast that kind of progress could move.

items.headline: Anthropic Blocks a Researcher Over Its Oldest Rule
items.excerpt: A researcher blamed a new Anthropic ban for his blocked account, but the rule against distillation predates Anthropic's October rewrite by months.

items.headline: David Durman Wins the Right to Skip AI
items.excerpt: A University of Kentucky research administrator's humanist beliefs now carry the same Title VII protection against mandatory AI use that courts already give traditional religions.

items.headline: Buyouts, Blocks and a Billion-Dollar Bet
items.excerpt: Microsoft offers 60,000 workers an exit, Anthropic blocks a researcher, and investors stop believing everyone's AI math on the same day.

items.headline: Cognition's Price Jumps While Model Gains Shrink
items.excerpt: Investors value Cognition near $80 billion, and its own president says smarter models now move fewer new users than before.

items.headline: Commercial Brokers Trust AI With Everything but the Deal
items.excerpt: Two-thirds of commercial real estate professionals use AI every week, but the richest firms are the only ones buying the data that earns real trust.

items.headline: Startups Beat AI Labs in Four of Five Categories
items.excerpt: Ramp's card data names Claude Code, Granola and Wispr Flow the top sellers in their categories, and startups beat the giant labs almost everywhere else.

items.headline: Blanchett Asks a Judge to Make AI Pay
items.excerpt: Cate Blanchett's coalition told a federal judge Hollywood can already license AI training, countering OpenAI's fair-use defense.

items.headline: Businesses Buy More AI as Top Spenders Pull Back
items.excerpt: Ramp's AI Index shows token prices down 51 percent since March, but the top 1 percent of spenders still trail their July peak.

items.headline: Google's Satellite Chip Clears Its Easiest Test
items.excerpt: Google's satellite wrote a haiku from orbit, but its own research says matching one data center on Earth needs 10,000 satellites.

items.headline: Anthropic's Alleged Mythos Leak Proves Fake
items.excerpt: A Hugging Face file claimed Anthropic's unreleased Mythos model had leaked, but the platform's own numbers and a reader's math proved the weights synthetic.

items.headline: Musk Says Grok Bot's Cost Outran Its Revenue
items.excerpt: Elon Musk said Grok Bot's running costs passed its revenue right as paying users hit sudden weekly limits.

items.headline: The Signal 2026-W44: Chip Billions Pile Up as OpenAI Trims Its War Chest
items.excerpt: Broadcom, Meta, and SpaceX struck 200 billion dollars in chip financing, OpenAI cut its raise to 20 billion dollars, and four labs agreed on one AI training opt out.
